extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer-algebra system (mathematicians, researchers, and students working with algebraic structures)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for creating and manipulating magmas, their elements, generating sets, substructures (submagmas, normal closures, ideals), quotients, and related homomorphisms in the Magma computer-algebra system. Covers input/output representation, naming, constructors, and mapping operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two families of category representations (input/output behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two families of magma categories with respect to input and output representation: (1) categories where elements have a concrete representation that does not explicitly display generators; (2) categories where elements are represented explicitly as expressions/words in the generators (free or finitely-presented magmas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In family (1) naming generators via a generator assignment statement assigns identifiers for convenience but does not affect appearance of output; in family (2) generator names appear explicitly in printed elements and generator assignment affects printing. Examples: GF(25) shows GF25.1 for generator (family 1); PolynomialRing prints variable names when created with R<x,y,z> (family 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use generator assignment to name generators
rubrics_metrics.description: A generator assignment statement (e.g., M<a,b> := ...) assigns generator identifiers to make input easier and output more readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming generators does not change underlying mathematical structure but affects how generators are referenced (M.i) and may change printnames in categories where output shows generators. Example: s5<a,b> := Sym(5); then b * a prints with the chosen names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default printing of generators (M.i and $.i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma's default method of printing the ith generator of a magma M is M.i; if it cannot locate an identifier for M it uses $.i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of $.i (pseudo-identifier) when a magma is unnamed or the identifier cannot be found; Generators(FreeMonoid(6)) prints { $.1, $.2, ... } but once assigned (FM6 := FreeMonoid(6)) generators print as FM6.1, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: AssignNames changes printnames but does not create identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: AssignNames(~M, Q) changes generator printnames for a magma in family (2) but does not create identifers with those names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After AssignNames(~A, ["k","l","m"]) the printed expressions use k,l,m, but inputs must still use A.i (e.g., A.1). To create identifiers the user must manually assign k := A.1, etc. Warning: reassigning the identifier (e.g., x := 17) may make printed names and identifiers diverge, potentially causing confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating submagmas, normal closures, and ideals (constructors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sub< M | specification_of_S >, ncl< M | specification_of_S >, and ideal< M | specification_of_S > to build submagma, normal closure, or ideal generated by S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The right-hand list may contain elements of M, sequences of primitives (literal element constructors), sets/sequences of elements, submagmas/ideals (interpreted as their generators), or sets/sequences of submagmas/ideals. If M has non-commutative multiplication and is not a group, ideal denotes two-sided ideal; left and right ideal constructors (lideal, rideal) exist. Examples: N<A,B>, i := sub<m23 | [ ... ], [ ... ]>.

rubrics_metrics.name: What may appear in generator specification S
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions on the right of the | in sub/ncl/ideal constructors may be: an element of M; a sequence of primitive objects interpreted as that element; a set/sequence of elements; a submagma or ideal (taken as its generators); or a set/sequence of submagmas/ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal expression syntax is allowed. Magma removes repeated elements and the identity element when processing the list; an empty or identity-only list returns the trivial substructure. Ordering is placed on generators so ith generator can be referred to as N.i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal and modification of listed generators
rubrics_metrics.description: When Magma processes the generator list it may remove repetitions, remove identity, and in some categories remove other redundant elements or replace elements with category-appropriate generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences include: Ngens may be smaller than the number of listed items; Generators(M) may contain fewer distinct elements than the constructor list; for ideals extra generators may be added; for polycyclic groups given elements may be replaced by pc-generators. Ordering of the final generators follows a modified version of the input list (with rules for sets and nested magmas). Examples illustrate repeats, zeros, or redundant entries being removed or adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators(M) and Ngens(M) semantics and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generators(M) returns the set of all generators of M; Ngens(M) or NumberOfGenerators(M) returns the count. These are elements of M. Exceptions exist when a category forces exactly one generator (use Generator(M) / M.1) or different naming like Rank(R) for polynomial ring indeterminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators is a set (unordered in print), but M.i gives ordered access to the ith generator. Beware that printed order of Generators(M) may not match M.i ordering (examples: Sym(5) printed set order vs M.1/M.2 shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreground vs background/internal generating sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma distinguishes between a foreground representation (used for input/output) and a background representation (used for computation), where internal generating sets chosen by algorithm designers (e.g., echelon basis, BSGS) may differ from user-facing generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should not assume internal generators or representations; Magma attempts to retain user's chosen representation for I/O, but algorithms may use more efficient internal generating sets for operations like membership tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of generators depends on construction method
rubrics_metrics.description: The way generators of M are determined and ordered depends on how M was constructed: (a) free magma (generators from context); (b) returned by a function constructing standard examples (algorithm-chosen); (c) built by sub/ncl/ideal constructor; (d) arising from other expressions (no general rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case (c) the final generator set relates to the constructor expressions but may be modified as noted (removal/replacement/added elements). If expressions are sensible and independent, M.i will correspond to them in order; otherwise behavior is category dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of locality (independence of substructure representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for ideals, a submagma N of M has a representation independent of M; N exists in its category in its own right and its elements are presented relative to N, not using M's representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means algorithms for the category apply to N directly. Practically, if M is a module of dimension n and T a submodule of dimension m, elements of T are presented with m components (the standard basis of K^m), not n components. To map elements back to M use the inclusion monomorphism or coercion (M ! t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion monomorphism returned by constructors (multiple return values)
rubrics_metrics.description: sub, ncl and ideal constructors (and relatives) can return two values: the substructure and the inclusion monomorphism i : N → M. The quo constructor similarly returns the natural homomorphism as its second value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple assignment to capture both return values: T, i := sub< M | ... >; if the constructor is used in an expression or single assignment only the substructure is returned. The homomorphism is useful to map sets, sequences or submagmas into the parent; coercion (M ! t) often suffices for single elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic(T) returns the free/generic magma embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic(T) returns the free or generic magma in which T is naturally embedded. If T was created as a substructure of M, Generic(T) equals Generic(M) unless M is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to determine the ultimate ambient magma; examples show symmetric group equality checks like s6 eq Generic(s6sub) returning true.

rubrics_metrics.name: quo-constructor for quotient magmas and homomorphism behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: quo< M | specification_of_S > constructs the quotient magma Q = M/I where I is the normal closure/ideal generated by S (rules for S same as sub/ncl/ideal). The constructor returns Q and the natural homomorphism φ : M → Q as its second return value when used with multiple assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have I assigned to an identifier first (so it can be inspected), create I := ncl< M | ... > and then use quo< M | I >. The natural homomorphism can be used to map elements, sets, and submagmas; preimages can be computed with @@. Note: quotient magma Q is not a substructure of M and may be represented in a different category (e.g., RngUPolRes for polynomial quotients). Kernel(n) returns the ideal used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient magma is not a substructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The quotient Q = M/I is represented separately and is not a substructure of M; representations and element formats (e.g., vector length or permutation degree) may differ between M and Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect differences in categories (e.g., polynomial quotient Pq is Univariate Quotient Polynomial Algebra with modulus; vector spaces get different component counts). Use the natural homomorphism to translate between structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorthand constructors for finitely-presented magmas
rubrics_metrics.description: For frequent construction of finitely-presented magmas there are shorthand constructors: constructor-word< generators | relations > for Group, Semigroup, Monoid, PolycyclicGroup, AbelianGroup, avoiding explicit construction of the free magma first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators are identifers used inside the constructor's scope; relations list equalities or words. The shorthand returns the natural homomorphism as a second return value when used in multiple assignment. Example: G<c,d> := Group< a, b | a^2, b^3, (a*b)^4 >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorthand constructors for submagmas of generic magmas
rubrics_metrics.description: For categories with generic magmas (matrix groups, matrix algebras, permutation groups, linear codes) there are shorthand constructors of the form constructor-word< generic_specification | generators > which produce a submagma of the generic magma in one step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The left-side generic specification uses the same arguments as the function that constructs the generic magma (e.g., MatrixGroup<3, K | ...> for GL(3,K)). The shorthand typically returns the inclusion monomorphism as the second return value. Examples: MatrixGroup<3, K | ...>, PermutationGroup< 9 | ... >, LinearCode< GF(2), 7 | Q >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior when constructing normal closures and ideals (addition of generators)
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing normal closures or ideals Magma often needs to enlarge the given generating set to obtain a substructure that is normal or an ideal in M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma will add extra generators and place them (usually) at the end of the generator list so that user-specified generators appear first. Example: ncl< s5 | (1,2,3), (1,3)(2,4) > resulted in Ngens = 3 with an added generator (3,5,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Magma operator and function summary for general magma operations
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of principal operators/functions applies to (nearly) all magmas: #M (cardinality or Order for groups), L eq M, L ne M, L cmpeq M, x in M, x notin M, L subset M, L notsubset M, L meet M, Rep(M), Random(M), Set(M), FormalSet(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use #M to obtain size of finite magma; Random(M) returns a random element; L meet M gives intersection; Order(M) is a synonym for #M when M is a group. Examples include #GF(2,4) -> 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element creation in finitely-presented/free categories
rubrics_metrics.description: In categories where magmas derive from abstract free structures (finitely-presented magmas, polynomial rings), elements are represented as expressions (words) in the generators. To create an element the user must express it explicitly in terms of generators or as combinations of previously-defined elements that were created in terms of generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators appear explicitly in printed elements, so generator assignment and printnames matter for readability. Example: in a polynomial ring created without names f prints with $.1 syntax, whereas R<x,y,z> prints with x,y,z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of coercion versus inclusion homomorphism for mapping elements
rubrics_metrics.description: To view an element of a substructure as an element of the parent magma, either apply the inclusion homomorphism i (if obtained) or use coercion via the parent (M ! t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining the inclusion homomorphism is convenient for mapping sets or sequences; coercion is simpler for single elements. Example: i(t) and M ! t produce the same element of M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special constructors for left/right ideals in non-group noncommutative contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: If M has non-commutative multiplication and is not a group, ideal denotes the two-sided ideal; left and right ideal constructors (lideal and rideal) are also available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate constructor depending on the kind of ideal you intend to build (two-sided, left, or right). See referenced example on p. 531 (in-document reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing order of Generators(M) may not match M.i ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which the set Generators(M) is printed does not necessarily correspond to the M.i ordering of the generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on generator indices (M.i) for input or programmatic manipulation, do not assume printed set order matches index order; use explicit M.i notation to be unambiguous. Examples: Sym(5) printed generator set order differs from s5.1, s5.2 outputs shown.
